clue.text: I wasn't upset by snake, being a naval officer

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake

indicators.note: upset says the letters of these words are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests they were not frightened by a snake, while serving as an officer aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like distress at the snake but is the anagram signal on I wasn't.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosun is the ship's officer in charge of rigging, boats and deck crew.

clue.text: See 20
A hat on the head of Peter Fitzgerald not accompanied

parts.note: a cap is a hat

indicators.note: the head of asks for the first letter of Peter

parts.note: Ella Fitzgerald was the American jazz singer

explanation.surface: A hat perched on the head of a man called Peter Fitzgerald, who is out on his own.
explanation.walkthrough: Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer, fittingly supplies part of a singing term.
explanation.definitionFit: Music sung a cappella is performed by voices alone, without instrumental backing.

clue.text: Accepts RAF version: could be a UFO

indicators.note: a version is a reworking, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: The Royal Air Force accepts an account of what might have been a flying saucer.
explanation.walkthrough: RAF is the Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: An unidentified flying object might be a vessel travelling through space, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Surprise about German joiner

parts.note: as to means about or concerning
und is German for and, a word that joins

explanation.surface: Amazement at a carpenter from Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' looks like a carpenter but is a conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound someone is to amaze them, a stronger synonym of surprise used as a verb.

clue.text: We French embracing axiom: being unclothed is bad for you

indicators.note: embracing means the French word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: nous is French for we

indicators.note: being unclothed strips the outer letters from the word axiom

explanation.surface: The French declare as a maxim that going naked is harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being unclothed' leaves XIO from aXIOm.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harmful or poisonous to health is a fair description of what is bad for you.

clue.text: Pope's first mass is full

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word Pope's

parts.note: a lump is a solid mass

explanation.surface: A remark that the Pope's first Mass of the day is well attended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like the church service but is just a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something rounded out and well filled, as in plump cushions.

clue.text: See 24
Employment for lami or veloy with parts missing?

indicators.note: with parts missing says the sausage loses the same opening piece the two printed words lost

parts.note: salami and saveloy are each a sausage, here printed with their opening SA missing

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what use there is for some mangled words.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed words are salami and saveloy without SA; treat sausage the same way. A saveloy is a seasoned British smoked sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something is used, so employment in the sense of putting to use.

clue.text: After exercise, breathless — nursed by outstanding teacher

indicators.note: After places the following material behind the exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education

indicators.note: nursed by means held inside the following word

parts.note: an outstanding bill is due, still unpaid
agog means breathless with eagerness

explanation.surface: After a workout, an exceptional teacher looks after someone panting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise but means owing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedagogue is a schoolmaster, often a pedantic one.

clue.text: Some horny Alaskan antelope

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nonsense image of a horned Alaskan antelope, though the animal belongs elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned southern African antelope.

clue.text: Cabaret for the audience?

parts.note: heard by listeners, the word cabaret is close to 'cab array', a line-up of cabs waiting for fares

explanation.surface: A question about what a nightclub show offers its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed answer, a feature of the urban landscape: Cabaret heard by an audience suggests 'cab array'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank where cabs line up waiting for fares is exactly an array of cabs.

clue.text: Bump into not quite happy ex reversing — no joke!

indicators.note: not quite asks for the phrase happy ex without all its letters, losing the Y and the X
reversing tells you to read the joke-free piece backwards

parts.note: a joke is a pun, so no joke gives no pun

explanation.surface: Someone runs into a former partner who is not quite happy, and it is no laughing matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' leaves HAPPE from HAPPY EX; 'reversing' turns NOPUN into NUPON.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into someone is to meet them by chance, an idiom for a chance encounter.

clue.text: Mountain where Ingrid lost her man

indicators.note: lost tells you that a piece is dropped from the actress's surname

parts.note: Ingrid Bergman was the Swedish star of Casablanca
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountain setting where the actress Ingrid lost her husband or lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop MAN from BERGMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Berg is German and Afrikaans for a hill or mountain, used in English for South African mountains and for icebergs.

clue.text: Part of brain that's extremely creative brewed beer to mull over

indicators.note: extremely asks for the outermost letters of creative
brewed says the letters of beer are stirred into a new order
over turns the word mull upside down in this down entry

explanation.surface: An inventive brewer thinks about a new beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' turns BEER into REBE; 'over' turns MULL into LLUM; CE comes from creativE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebellum is the region at the back of the brain that coordinates movement.

clue.text: Seduced everyone — awfully rude

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of rude are badly mangled

explanation.surface: Someone seduced the whole company and behaved terribly rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns RUDE into URED.
explanation.definitionFit: To allure is to tempt or entice, a close synonym for seduce.

clue.text: George a 27? Too bad!

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of these pieces are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: 27 refers to the answer at 27 across, a flower

explanation.surface: Someone named George is called a flower and dismisses that as too bad.
explanation.walkthrough: George is old RAF slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: George is British pilots' nickname for the automatic flight-control system.

clue.text: Entire operation of the female thrill

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
a bang is a thrill or kick, as in getting a bang out of something

explanation.surface: A woman's thrill described as the whole affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the whole shebang' means the entire thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebang is slang for an affair or business, found in the idiom the whole shebang.

clue.text: Herbal medicine makes a pedant go berserk

indicators.note: going berserk means going wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy drives a fussy scholar into a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaptogen is a plant substance claimed to help the body resist stress, sold as a herbal supplement.

clue.text: Cars few and far between

parts.note: cars on the road are traffic
light means sparse, as in light traffic

explanation.surface: Sparse traffic, with cars few and far between.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed answer, a feature of the urban landscape, with no separate definition: the whole clue is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Street furniture theme: a road signal, built from a phrase meaning sparse traffic.

clue.text: Precipitating a change of leader in having a rest

indicators.note: a change of leader in says the first letter of the resting word is swapped for another

parts.note: pausing means stopping for a rest

explanation.surface: Someone resting brings on a change of leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the P of PAUSING for C.
explanation.definitionFit: To precipitate an event is to bring it about suddenly, a sense shared with making happen.

clue.text: Mean street, right time

parts.note: Ave is the abbreviation for avenue, a street
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A rough street at the right time, as if setting a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective for a rough street but is the arithmetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of numbers is their arithmetic average.

clue.text: Marsh fens half-stripped of weapons

indicators.note: stripped asks for each word with its outer letters peeled off

explanation.surface: Weapons found in fenland marsh, half stripped bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' leaves ARS, EN and AL from mARSh, fENs and hALf.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store of weapons, so the word stands for the weapons it holds.

clue.text: Green judges

parts.note: a green is a public park
the bench is the collective term for judges

explanation.surface: Inexperienced judges.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed answer, a feature of the urban landscape, with no separate definition: the whole clue is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Street furniture theme: a seat in a public garden, built from green space and a seat for judges.

clue.text: Rise in 13

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the brain part at 13, so its outer letters are dropped

parts.note: 13 points to the answer at 13 down, a part of the brain

explanation.surface: A rise inside the brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' asks for the word sitting within ceREBELlum, the answer to 13 down.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise up against authority is to revolt, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Cracker keeps the Financial Times quiet

definitions.text: Cracker keeps the Financial Times quiet

indicators.note: keeps means the cracker holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a belter or a cracker is an outstanding example of something
the newspaper refers to itself as us
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A cracking story keeps the Financial Times quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed answer, a feature of the urban landscape, with no separate definition. 'the Financial Times' is US because this puzzle appears in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Street furniture theme: a roadside cover where commuters wait, built entirely from wordplay.

clue.text: Up and down and round it goes

indicators.note: Up and down says the letters read the same either way in this down entry

parts.note: a spinning ... goes round

explanation.surface: A description of something going up, down and around.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning part of a machine, like a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: Light job

parts.note: a lamp is a light
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: An easy job.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed answer, a feature of the urban landscape, with no separate definition: the whole clue is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Street furniture theme: a standard holding a street light, built from a light and a job.

clue.text: Bookish type, one born at the end of September, back in his element? On the contrary!

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
On the contrary says the reverse holds: the element goes inside the person, not him inside it

parts.words: one born at the end of September
parts.note: a Libran is born under Libra, the star sign covering late September

indicators.note: back says the element is written in reverse

parts.note: Libra is an air sign, so air is a Libran's element

explanation.surface: A bookish Libran is happiest back in his element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the element, and 'On the contrary' flips 'in': the element goes inside the person rather than him in it. Libra is an air sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper of books in a library is the bookish type par excellence.

clue.text: See 17
Some advice given about essentially peculiar flower

indicators.note: given about means the advice is wrapped round the next piece

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice

indicators.note: essentially asks for the central letters of peculiar

explanation.surface: Advice is offered about a strange flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' gives UL, the core of pecULiar.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a bulb-grown spring bloom.

clue.text: Mingled or mixed-up fortune hunter

indicators.note: mixed-up says the letters of the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A confused, mingled-up fortune hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospector digging for gold is literally hunting a fortune.
